correctness.rationale: Exact diagonalization of the averaging matrix yields the first pair of Fourier modes and ellipse semiaxes. Uniform sample quantile-process weak convergence, a globally uniform Taylor remainder and bridge integration by parts yield a circular Gaussian with independent coordinate variances 1/8; the two distribution constants follow algebraically. Rotation symmetry proves exact finite-n direction independence. The standalone checker confirms matrix-SVD and midpoint identities and performs corroborative finite-sample diagnostics. The only limits claimed are in distribution at n→∞ after fixed-n spectral identification.

value.rationale: For a natural and precisely motivated random input to a classical polygon-smoothing process, the theorem identifies the previously unevaluated shape-statistic law. The distinct \(n^{-1/2}\) axis mismatch and \(n^{-1/4}\) geometric eccentricity, with an explicit quartic-Weibull distribution and exact finite-n directional symmetry, are structural rather than arbitrary parameter refinements.
